newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Active bids, offers sparked trades.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Active bids, offers sparked trades.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was active on Friday with at least three cargoes changing hands and traders said they expected the active trade to continue in the near term.
Two 380-cst grade cargoes were traded at $95 per tonne for mid-July lifting and one 180-cst cargo was traded at $100 per tonne, also for mid-July lifting, traders said.
"Majors are pretty keen in selling and buying interest is still there," said one trader, expecting the 180-cst grade to stay at above the $100-per-tonne level.
There have been some Chinese buying interests recently and traders said they expected the healthy enquiries to continue.
"The Chinese are asking for as high as $9 per tonne above Singapore spot quotes, which is good," one trader said.
The spread between the 180-cst grade and the 380-cst grade used to be at around $6.50/$7.00 but as the gas oil market was bearish, traders said the spread between the two grades is narrowing.
On Thursday, the 180-cst grade was traded at $98.50 per tonne and the 380-cst was done at $96 per tonne.
The spread rose to $5 per tonne on Friday.
On Friday, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) 30,000-tonne fuel oil cargoes at $3 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes, a CPC source said.
The 3.0-percent, 180-centistoke grade cargoes are for lifting in the second half of this year on a free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung basis, the source said.
The LSWR market was still waiting for allocation details from Indonesia's state oil firm Pertamina, which has initially decided to allocate 2.3 million barrels in July, traders said.
Pertamina allocated 3.1 million barrels in June, with additional 500,000 barrels rolled over from May.
"In any case, LSWR prices will just go up," said one trader, noting increasing summer demand from Japan.
On the SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, July was traded $1
down to $99.00, with 15 100-tonne lots traded.
